name: Paul R. Berger

family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Midwest/Boston upbringing.

The 1987 self-assembly claim lacks strong independent second sourcing and the biography carries a conflict-of-interest flag. No clear material independent milestone dated at age ≤26.

name: David Baszucki
milestone_by_age_26: In July 1989 at age 26 he co-founded Knowledge Revolution with his brother Greg and shipped Interactive Physics, a 2D educational physics simulator that became widely used in classrooms (company later acquired by MSC Software in 1998 for ~$20M).
early_history_summary: Born Winnipeg to Helen and Paul Baszucki (Ukrainian-Canadian immigrant descent); raised in Eden Prairie, Minnesota; high-school quiz-bowl captain and multi-sport student. Stanford BS electrical engineering 1985 (GM Scholar) with GM summer internship on software-controlled engines. After Stanford, built physics-simulation software and founded Knowledge Revolution in 1989.
family_context_summary: Born to Helen and Paul Baszucki who met at University of Saskatchewan; Ukrainian immigrant family roots in western Canada; raised in suburban Eden Prairie, Minnesota.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parental occupations beyond university-educated immigrant background not documented as software/engineering domain apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford EE, brother Greg cofounder, Macintosh-era physics software, educational market immersion, Interactive Physics
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Roblox IR board bio agree he founded Knowledge Revolution from July 1989 (age 26) and built Interactive Physics; MSC acquisition ~$20M in 1998 is independently reported (Forbes, Wikipedia). Stanford EE + sibling cofounder concentrated execution; family domain transfer into software is not documented. Later Roblox (2004–06 launch, 2021 IPO) made him a billionaire operator.
starting_point: Born 20 January 1963 in Winnipeg to university-educated Ukrainian-Canadian parents; raised in Eden Prairie, Minnesota; Stanford electrical engineering graduate (1985).
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Roblox Corporation; Forbes-estimated multi-billion net worth (~$5.6B as of Dec 2025); leads Baszucki Group philanthropy with wife Jan Ellison.

trajectory.event: Graduated Stanford as General Motors Scholar in electrical engineering after a GM software-engine internship.
Co-founded Knowledge Revolution with brother Greg and released Interactive Physics educational simulator.
Sold Knowledge Revolution to MSC Software for about $20 million; later served as VP/GM.
Began prototyping what became Roblox with Erik Cassel (eBlocks/DynaBlocks era).
Officially released Roblox as a user-generated 3D game platform.
Roblox listed on NYSE; personal wealth and philanthropy (Baszucki Group/brain research) scaled dramatically.

name: James W. Hunt
milestone_by_age_26: In 1976 at age 23–24 he co-authored with Douglas McIlroy the Bell Labs technical report 'An Algorithm for Differential File Comparison' (Hunt–McIlroy algorithm), foundational to Unix diff; in 1977 (age 24–25) he published the Hunt–Szymanski LCS algorithm in Communications of the ACM.
early_history_summary: Born Trenton, NJ, to Augustus and Bernyce Hunt; first of two children. B.S. electrical engineering cum laude from Princeton; M.S. and Ph.D. electrical engineering from Stanford; early NSBE chapter member. Work on diff prototypes and LCS algorithms while young produced algorithms still used in version control, wikis, and phylogenetics software. Later led groups at Bell Labs, UNIX System Laboratories, and Lucent.
family_context_summary: Born to Augustus and Bernyce Hunt in Trenton, New Jersey; African-American family; detailed wealth/class not documented beyond path into Princeton/Stanford.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a computer-science domain apprenticeship in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Princeton EE, Stanford EE PhD path, Bell Labs collaboration with McIlroy, Hunt-Szymanski CACM, African-American pioneer path
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, Bell Labs CTR 41 (Hunt & McIlroy 1976 PDF), and 1977 CACM Hunt–Szymanski paper independently date the algorithms at ages 23–25. Princeton/Stanford pipeline and McIlroy collaboration concentrated opportunity; family domain transfer into CS not documented. Later Bell Labs/USL/Lucent executive career and patents extend the trajectory until death in 2021.
starting_point: Born 5 August 1952 in Trenton, New Jersey, to Augustus and Bernyce Hunt; African-American first child who pursued elite EE education at Princeton then Stanford.
current_position: Died 21 March 2021 at age 68; final major industry roles included Management Systems Product Realization VP at Lucent Technologies (retired 2004); remembered for foundational diff/LCS algorithms.

trajectory.event: Co-authored Hunt–McIlroy differential file comparison technical report with Douglas McIlroy at Bell Labs—core of Unix diff.
Published Hunt–Szymanski fast LCS algorithm in Communications of the ACM.
Published IEEE Computer survey article on programming languages.
Retired after decade-plus leadership path through Bell Labs, UNIX System Laboratories, and Lucent Technologies.
Died March 21, 2021; remembered as African-American computer scientist and inventor behind widely used differencing algorithms.

current_position: Principal Cloud Advocate at Microsoft/GitHub; former Khan Academy CS curriculum creator, Coursera early engineer, Google DevRel, and UC Berkeley lecturer.

Joined Coursera as an early frontend/full-stack engineer after ~5 years at Google.
Moved into engineering and CS education content creation at Khan Academy (Hour of Code era and multi-year curriculum work).
Taught/lectured computer science at UC Berkeley while continuing education-product work.
Joined Microsoft as a Cloud Developer Advocate (later GitHub-facing advocacy), publishing widely on Python and AI coding agents.

name: Paul Graham (programmer)
milestone_by_age_26: Cornell BA 1986 (age ~21), Harvard MS 1988 and PhD 1990 (age ~25–26). Viaweb cofounded 1996 (age 31), On Lisp 1994 (age ~29), Y Combinator 2005 (age 40). Completing a CS PhD by ~26 is ordinary academic progress, not a material independent career milestone under this rubric.
early_history_summary: Born Weymouth, England; father designed nuclear reactors for Westinghouse; family moved to Pittsburgh 1968. Coded in high school; Cornell philosophy BA; Harvard CS MS/PhD; also studied painting at RISD and Florence. Major breakout was Viaweb then YC essays/investing.
family_context_summary: Father from Wales worked designing nuclear reactors for Westinghouse; family relocated from England to Pittsburgh.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a nuclear-reactor engineer—technical professional background but not software entrepreneurship apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Library of Congress authority file fix birth 13 Nov 1964; Harvard PhD 1990; Viaweb 1996 sale to Yahoo 1998; YC 2005. Strict age≤26 bar excludes him despite later legendary impact—fame and material founder milestones arrived in early 30s+.
